text:
Maya (Support): FYI ACME reported a regression overnight — their summarization endpoint is returning much shorter, 'safe' replies. They say it started right after our 23:45 UTC rollout.

Deepak (Eng): Do we have a repro sample from them? any request payload they shared?

Maya (Support): They pasted this minimal repro (customer says they didn't set sampling fields explicitly):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"summarize-v2","input":"<long doc>","max_tokens":150}'
```
Output used to be ~3 short paragraphs; now it's a one-liner.

Priya (ML): That smell like sampling defaults drift. If temp/top_p got set low globally, requests without explicit overrides will become deterministic/abridged. Can someone check config/audit? :mag:

deploy-bot: CONFIG_UPDATE detected 2026-03-16T23:45:12Z by rollout-service (job id: deploy-2026-03-16-445). Changed param: `/service/serving/default_sampling` from `\{"temperature\":0.9,\"top_p\":0.95\}` to `\{"temperature\":0.0,\"top_p\":0.1\}`.

Jon (SRE): Confirmed in audit logs and parameter store. SSM path: /prod/redwood/serving/default_sampling. Change_id: c9b2f. Caller: rollout-service@ci.

Deepak (Eng): Oof. Was that an intentional opt-in for any new deterministic rollout? I don't recall approving a global default change.

Priya (ML): Not intentional for broad rollout. We had an experiment to stabilize outputs for a specific internal customer but it should've been tenant-scoped. Looks like the rollout manifest used the prod/global path by mistake.

Maya (Support): ACME is asking for ETA to fix and whether we can revert to previous behavior. They have high traffic and this affects their UX.

Jon (SRE): Quick mitigation paths: 1) rollback param to previous value, 2) set an override for ACME tenant, or 3) advise them to pass explicit sampling keys in their requests. I'll do rollback now if eng confirms.

Deepak (Eng): Proceed with rollback asap. Use this command to restore the previous defaults (will take effect in ~30s):
```bash
aws ssm put-parameter --name /prod/redwood/serving/default_sampling \
  --value '{"temperature":0.9,"top_p":0.95}' --type String --overwrite --region us-west-2
```

Priya (ML): Also add a quick guard: reject future deploys that attempt to write global sampling without the feature flag `sampling.global-allowed=true`. I'll open a PR after rollback.

Jon (SRE): Rolling back now. Will monitor rolling config refresh across frontends.

deploy-bot: ROLLBACK completed 2026-03-16T23:52:03Z for change_id c9b2f -> restored previous sampling defaults.

Maya (Support): I informed ACME: we're rolling back and will follow up with a timeline + postmortem. They asked for repro guidance in the meantime; shared this quick snippet they can use to force the previous behavior client-side:
```json
{"temperature":0.9, "top_p":0.95}
```

Deepak (Eng): Action items:
- Priya: PR to add feature-flag guard + unit tests (owner: Priya)
- Jon: Add alert on sudden global sampling param changes (owner: Jon)
- Deepak: Postmortem + change to rollout playbook to prevent accidental global paths (owner: Deepak)

Priya (ML): For the postmortem, I'll include a small repro harness that compares output length distribution and token-per-response before/after any sampling config change. Quick check: ACME's avg tokens/response dropped from ~420 -> ~48 after the change (from metrics).

Maya (Support): Thanks. I'll keep the ticket updated and confirm with ACME once we have the postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:

Jon (SRE): I'll also add a temporary policy to block rollout-service from writing that SSM path until we have the change approved.

Maya (Support): Closing loop for now — thanks everyone. We'll track follow-ups in the postmortem thread.
